To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequency of miniature acetylcholine potentials (m.e.P.P.) at the neuromotor junction is increased when calcium ion concentration is reduced, and is increased when the calcium ion concentration is increased, and is increased by increasing the calcium ion concentration.

the rate of miniature end- plate potential production at the neuromu scular junction in the rat diaphrag m is dependent upon calcium and that calcium-dependent miniature end-plate potential production is facilitated by a reduction in magnesium concentration.

calcium ions are required for spontaneous acetylcholinesterase release at mammalian neuromotor terminals, but that the rate of release is not directly proportional to the concentration of extracellular calcium ions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the effect of calcium on the production of m.e.p.p.s.
the calcium dependence of spontaneous release of ACh quanta from the phrenic nerve terminals of the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium dependence of spontaneous acetycholine release at the mammalian motor end-plate is not due to a calcium requirement for vesicle fusion with the presynaptic membrane.
Ca2+ is not necessary for the release of ACh at mammalian neuromascular junctions.

(1) calcium is essential for spontaneous release of ACh; (2) the release of ACh quanta is not affected by increasing Mg2+ concentration; (3) the release of quants of ACh is not affected by exposure to EDTA; (4) the release of quantal ACh is affected by increasing external Ca2+ concentration; and (5) the release of spontaneous ACh quanta may be facilitated by the presence of Ca2+ in the bathing solution
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the rat, Ca2+ is required for spontaneous ACh release at the motor nerve terminal.
the m.e.p.ps of the rat are dependent on Ca2+ in the bathing medium and that this dependency can be altered by changing the ionic strength and/or pH of the medium.
, in the rat, the production of m.e.p.p.s is dependent on Ca2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calcium-dependent mechanism of ACh release is not the only one at work.
the presence of calcium in the extracellular fluid is necessary for the production of miniature end-plates at mammalian motor end-plates.
, in the absence of Ca2+, the rate of m.e.p.p.s can be greatly increased by increasing the Ca2+ concentration in the bathing solution.
